newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to allow electronic prospectuses.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to allow electronic prospectuses.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Wednesday it would allow the use of electronic prospectuses from October 1.
The decision was part of a larger trend towards electronic commerce and would help reduce distribution costs, ASC regulatory policy director Shane Tregillis said in a statement.

"The electronic prospectus policy is part of the ASC's continuing efforts to facilitate electronic commerce developments in the finanacial services industry while maintaining the confidence of investors in the integrity of the Australian capital markets," Tregillis said.
From October 1 the ASC will provide class order relief to allow all companies and managers to distribute electronic prospectuses.

Companies must also lodge a paper prospectus with the ASC, the electronic prospectus must provide the same information as the paper example and companies must take steps to protect the electronic prospectus from tampering.

Some differences will be allowed between paper and electronic prospectuses, including the use of prompts to encourage investors to read the prospectus, an electronic dictionary of words used and links to other documents.
"Electronic prospectuses may also lead to better use of prospectuses by investors and wider access to investment products," Tregillis said.
"Electronic commerce will fundamentally affect the financial services industry during the next five years," he said.
"These changes may produce efficiencies in mobilising domestic and international savings and cheaper investment products that better meet the needs of investors."
